 Follow us on Facebook Twitter Hello Soccer MLS LaLiga World Cup Premier League Champions League CONCACAF Champions USWNT Serie A Bundesliga Ligue 1 Liga mexicana Europa League Argentina Boca Juniors vs. River Plate: Who are the young stars set to shine in the Superclásico?
 Boca Juniors are enjoying a remarkable resurgence, with Leonel Flores leading a new generation of talent ahead of today’s Superclásico against River Plate.
 Antonio Lacerda Víctor Martín J. twitter David Nelson twitter Update: Nov 1st, 2026 08:42 EST 0 Share facebook twitter whatsapp Make us preferred on Google Bo ca Juniors are enjoying one of their most exciting periods in years. With several trophies still up for grabs as the season enters its final stretch, including the Copa Sudamericana, where they have reached the final, there is plenty for the club’s supporters to celebrate. But beyond the prospect of silverware, one of the biggest reasons for optimism is the strength of the squad assembled under Rodolfo Arruabarrena. Alongside established stars such as Leandro Paredes, Miguel Merentiel, Lautaro Blanco and Santiago Ascacíbar, an exciting generation of young players is emerging, establishing itself in the starting lineup and attracting attention from Europe’s biggest clubs. 
 Players such as Lautaro Di Lollo, Leonel Flores, Facundo “Jagger” Herrera, Dylan Gorosito and Milton Delgado are now among Argentine soccer’s most promising prospects. Their emergence has put Boca at the forefront of the country’s talent production after several years in which bitter rivals River Plate dominated the market. While River previously commanded enormous transfer fees for players such as Enzo Fernández, Julián Álvarez, Claudio Echeverri and Franco Mastantuono, European clubs are now turning their attention to the latest jewels emerging from Boca’s academy. 
 Boca Juniors’ next generation: A dream and a sure thing
 Hugo Perotti, father of former Sevilla star Diego Perotti, is a living part of Boca Juniors’ history. A cult hero at the club during the 1970s and 1980s, he subsequently worked in its scouting department after retiring from playing. During his time identifying young talent, he helped bring through several players who have gone on to establish themselves in professional soccer. 
 “Varela, Medina, Capaldo, Balerdi, who’s in the Argentina national team, Almada and Flores himself all came through during my time at the club. Those are the youngest players who have made it into professional soccer. The players who are still emerging now, you could say, are products of our work,” Perotti told AS.
 Hugo 'Mono' Perotti with Maradona. In the interview, Perotti assessed Boca’s most promising youngsters and identified one player who, in his opinion, is already fully prepared to make the leap to European soccer. 
 “The player who’s genuinely established and ready to go to Europe is Milton Delgado. He’s already spent a couple of years playing regularly in the first division. He’s had to fight for his place, he’s been dropped, and he’s won his spot back. Flores is still going through that process, although he’s more attractive because he’s an attacking player, and that’s more valuable and eye-catching. That’s how it works everywhere in the world.”
 If Delgado is the safest bet, Flores is undoubtedly Boca’s biggest sensation right now. Perotti recognizes the young winger’s extraordinary potential, although his years of experience working with emerging talents have taught him to be cautious about predicting future success.
 “Flores dazzles you with his play. He’s fearless, incredibly technical and very clever. If he can maintain that level, he’ll become a problem for everyone. He has the potential to reach Europe’s biggest clubs, but it depends on him being professional and staying focused on his goals.”
 JUAN MABROMATA And Boca’s current crop of youngsters may still have more surprises in store. Perotti believes that some players develop later than others, sometimes emerging as outstanding professionals despite having spent much of their academy careers in the background.
 “There are youngsters who still haven’t broken through. It’s quite common for players to spend their entire development years on the bench and then become very important, because they grow and develop qualities they didn’t have as kids. Gago is a great example. He was a substitute in many of the youth categories, and look what he became. He ended up playing for Real Madrid,” the former Boca player explained.
 His assessment offers even more reasons for Boca supporters to be optimistic about the club’s future. 
 Finally, Perotti emphasized the importance of having an experienced figure like Leandro Paredes in the squad. The Argentine international has returned to Boca in excellent form, and his presence provides invaluable guidance both on and off the field. 
 “Having experienced players is essential. I was lucky enough to have role models when I made my debut, and they gave me some great advice. Those leaders are necessary, especially at big clubs that are under as much scrutiny as Boca.”
 Who are Boca Juniors’ most promising young players?
 Lautaro Di Lollo: The complete Argentine defender
 Di Lollo represents the traditional strengths of Argentine defending at their very best. The young center back has established himself as an extremely reliable presence at the heart of a top-level defense. His maturity at such a young age allows him to read the game exceptionally well, controlling space and timing with the composure of a much more experienced player.
 His defensive qualities, combined with his impressive aerial ability, make him a remarkably complete player. He is also a threat from set pieces, adding another dimension to Boca’s attacking options. 
 Milton Delgado: The midfielder ready for Europe
 An energetic, tireless talent, the 21-year-old midfielder combines technical quality with an exceptional ability to cover ground. Delgado is a complete player who contributes across the entire midfield, offering both defensive security and attacking support. 
 Playing alongside a deep-lying playmaker of Paredes’ caliber has helped make Boca’s midfield arguably the strongest in Argentine soccer. Delgado’s versatility and all-around ability make him an ideal complement to more creative players, while also establishing him as an attractive prospect for European clubs. 
 Facundo “Jagger” Herrera: Strength and elegance in defense
 A combination of physical presence and technical sophistication, Herrera has one of the most memorable nicknames in world soccer, thanks to his resemblance to Rolling Stones frontman Mick Jagger.
 Lautaro Di Lollo (L) celebrates with his teammate Boca Juniors' defender #42 Facundo Herrera. MAURO PIMENTEL But the Boca defender has far more to offer than an eye-catching nickname. Comfortable playing out from the back, composed in defensive situations and physically imposing when necessary, Herrera combines elegance with the toughness required of a modern center back. 
 His ability to handle one-on-one situations and his considerable room for improvement suggest that his full potential is still some way from being realized.
 Dylan Gorosito: Boca’s relentless competitor
 Gorosito may not possess the eye-catching technical qualities of some of his fellow prospects, but few players demonstrate greater determination when wearing Boca’s famous blue and gold jersey.
 A physically imposing defender, he is the kind of relentless opponent who can make life miserable for even the most accomplished forwards. 
 His intensity, competitive mentality and willingness to fight for every ball are qualities that could turn him into an extremely valuable player in the years ahead.
 Leonel Flores: The jewel in Boca’s crown
 Flores is the standout talent of Boca’s emerging generation, a young winger whose explosive ability has already made him one of Argentine soccer’s most exciting prospects. 
 Fearless, lightning-fast and seemingly unstoppable when running at defenders, Flores possesses the kind of natural talent that can transform a game in an instant.
 He is still developing his understanding of the game and refining the role he wants to play, but that only makes his potential more intriguing. 
 For Boca, Flores represents a breath of fresh air and a symbol of the club’s exciting future. For Europe’s biggest clubs, he is rapidly becoming one of the most attractive young prospects on the market.
